issue_context.title: Import error when using package imports in vite.config.js
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When I use [package imports](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest/api/packages.html#subpath-imports) in `vite.config.js`,  Vite fails to load the configuration file and displays the following error:

```
failed to load config from .../vite.config.js
error when starting dev server:
TypeError [ERR_PACKAGE_IMPORT_NOT_DEFINED]: Package import specifier "#src/utils.js" is not defined imported from .../node_modules/.vite-temp/vite.config.ts.timestamp-1733215455982-e048dc6e2c576.mjs
```

This used to work in v5. My best guess is that it is caused by https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18509.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-aszvug?file=package.json

### Steps to reproduce

```
pnpm install
npx vite
```



### System Info

```shell
  System:
    OS: Linux 5.0 undefined
    CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz
    Memory: 0 Bytes / 0 Bytes
    Shell: 1.0 - /bin/jsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 18.20.3 - /usr/local/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.19 - /usr/local/bin/yarn
    npm: 10.2.3 - /usr/local/bin/npm
    pnpm: 8.15.6 - /usr/local/bin/pnpm
  npmPackages:
    vite: ^6.0.2 => 6.0.2 
```


### Used Package Manager

pnpm

### Logs

_No response_

comments: Looks like any files placed in `node_modules` can't access subpath imports from the root package.json, which is strange and I don't see it particularly documented in node. Anyways I guess we have to resolve subpath imports as well to fix this.
It looks like #18637 would solve this since it doesn't rely on the temporary file inside `node_modules` anymore.

Spec wise, probably Node bans this since `LOOKUP_PACKAGE_SCOPE` cuts off early for files under `node_modules`. I'm reading `PACKAGE_IMPORTS_RESOLVE` and `LOOKUP_PACKAGE_SCOPE` in https://nodejs.org/docs/v22.12.0/api/esm.html#resolution-algorithm-specification.

review_comments: `resolveByViteResolver` uses `tryNodeResolve` and `tryNodeResolve` does not resolve imports fields. Resolving imports field in `resolveByViteResolver` can also fix the reported issue. But typescript files referenced by imports field doesn't work with that fix (I guess this didn't work from before though). I made imports field to be bundled instead to allow typescript files to be referenced by imports field.
